summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with symptoms of uremia including weakness, nausea, itching, and fatigue due to end-stage renal disease and allograft failure. Her labs showed elevated BUN and creatinine with metabolic acidosis and hypokalemia. A tunneled dialysis catheter was placed in the left internal jugular vein, and she underwent three hemodialysis sessions during the admission, leading to clinical improvement. Her symptoms resolved, and labs stabilized. She was transitioned to outpatient dialysis, with medications adjusted including discontinuation of sodium bicarbonate and initiation of Nephrocaps and post-dialysis levetiracetam. Follow-up was arranged with nephrology, vascular surgery for fistula planning, and pain management. She was discharged home with home health services and clear instructions on weight monitoring and medication management.
problems: End stage renal disease with allograft failure
History of cerebrovascular accident complicated by seizures
Hemiplegia and hemiparesis following cerebral infarction affecting left non-dominant side
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
